To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a hot and dilate nuclear droplet is unstable to spinodal decomposition at high temperatures, (ii) the spinodal decomposition leads to the formation of fragments with a mass distribution that is very similar to that of fragments in multifragmentation experiments, and (iii) dissipation reduces the growth rates of unstable modes but does not affect the area in the ($\rho$,T)-space where spinodal decomposition occurs.
